Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

EarthFlux 0.1.0.9000 (development version)

Documentation

  • citation("EarthFlux") and CITATION.cff give the Zenodo DOI of the package (concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23981325, which resolves to the latest release; 0.1.0 is 10.5281/zenodo.23981326), and the README shows how to cite it.

  • The maps of the README and of the Example scene: Cauquenes article are shown in geographic coordinates (EPSG:4326); the computations stay on the native MODIS grid.

EarthFlux 0.1.0

First release of EarthFlux. It is experimental and not for operational or scientific production use: no result has been validated yet, and interfaces may change. The integrated earthflux() workflow, its presets, the automatic download of MODIS products, elevation models and weather forcing, and validation results are not part of this release.

Verification

  • Reference evapotranspiration (FAO-56, worked examples 18 and 19 reproduced; ASCE-EWRI 2005), unit conversions and MODIS product facts are VERIFICADA against their primary sources.
  • Most METRIC formulations are VERIFICADA (SEBAL-Idaho 2002): checked, with page and equation, against the SEBAL Idaho manual of the METRIC authors (Waters et al., 2002); the Perrier roughness against Allen et al. (2012, IAHS Publ. 352). The cross-check with Allen, Tasumi & Trezza (2007) remains desirable.
  • The stable momentum correction at the blending height is psi_m(200 m) = -5 (2 / L) (Eq. 38), so ef_h_control() defaults stable_psi_m_height to 2 m; the verified heights (200, 0.1 and 2 m) and c_p = 1004 J kg-1 K-1 are defaults too. The Monin-Obukhov length uses the surface temperature and g = 9.81 m s-2 (Eq. 34).
  • Still CANDIDATA, as explicit arguments without defaults: the partitioned shortwave transmissivity, the terrain projection of the incoming shortwave radiation, the incidence angle on a tilted plane, G of Tasumi, the FAO-56 air density in METRIC, the anchor selection criteria and ef_lambda(method = "metric"). Open: the temperature of the incoming longwave radiation (ef_rl_in()) and the emissivity of non-vegetated pixels (lai_nonveg). The register is dev/VERIFICATION.md in the source repository.

New features

  • METRIC core. The chain as numeric functions, from solar geometry to daily actual ET: radiation components and ef_net_radiation(), soil heat flux (ef_g()), anchor pixels (ef_select_anchors(), ef_anchors(), ef_anchor_conditions()), roughness, wind, friction velocity and aerodynamic resistance (ef_zom(), ef_ustar(), ef_rah()), the dT calibration and sensible heat (ef_calibrate_h(), ef_sensible_heat()), latent heat and ET (ef_latent_heat(), ef_et_inst(), ef_etrf(), ef_et_daily()).
  • Method families. Each family has a dispatcher with an explicit method and no default (e.g. ef_g(method = "bastiaanssen")), returning a classed object with the value, the method, diagnostic flags and provenance; the method functions return plain numerics.
  • Meteorological forcing. Weather station tables (ef_station_table()) with quality control (ef_station_qc()), derived variables verified against FAO-56 (vapour pressure, dew point, psychrometric constant, wind at 2 m, extraterrestrial and clear-sky radiation) and reference ET at the stations (ef_ref_et(), ef_station_ref_et()).
  • Spatial regionalization. ef_regionalize() maps a station variable onto the working grid by a representative station, global regression, inverse distance weighting or geographically weighted regression on an internal GWR core (ef_gwr_fit(), ef_gwr_predict()), with exact block prediction, spatial block cross-validation (ef_spatial_folds(), ef_regionalize_cv()) and optional parallel execution under a future plan.
  • MODIS surface state (internal, not exported yet): reading of local MODIS files, scaling, QA bits as flags, view time to UTC, broadband albedo and emissivity, temporal matching and aggregation to the native 1 km grid of the land surface temperature.
  • Example data. cauquenes_modis: the MODIS surface state of the Cauquenes province (Maule Region, Chile) on 15 February 2019.

Changes

  • Results are flagged, never silently corrected: one registry of diagnostic flags per stage (69 codes), classed conditions for errors and warnings.
  • Physical constants are defined once, with unit, source and verification status.
  • End-to-end tests run synthetic scenes through the METRIC chain, the forcing and the MODIS surface state.
  • EarthFlux imports terra, future, future.apply and stats; GWmodel is suggested for the cross-verification of the GWR core.

Documentation

  • README with the status of the release and an example on cauquenes_modis; introductory vignette; website articles Design and development status and Example scene: Cauquenes.
  • pkgdown site at https://djwillichile.github.io/EarthFlux/.
  • Continuous integration on Linux, Windows and macOS; GitHub releases built from the version tag; Zenodo archive of each release.
